candidates.label: Crete and Cyrene (Roman province, capital Gortyn, label point)
candidates.support: The province joined the island of Crete with Cyrene on the North African coast. The label point is Wikidata's point for the province, at Gortyn on Crete, its capital. Pleiades' representative point for the province, from its Barrington Atlas location, was not used because it lies offshore.

summary.text: Crete and Cyrene was a senatorial province joining the island of Crete with Cyrene and its territory on the North African coast, with its capital at Gortyn on Crete. Of this project's places only Crete, which Paul's ship sailed along on the voyage to Rome, lies in it. Cyrene is not one of this project's places, but the New Testament names it several times: Simon, who was compelled to carry Jesus' cross, was 'a man of Cyrene,' and Acts mentions 'the parts of Libya around Cyrene.'

history.text: Rome annexed Crete in 67 BC and joined it with Cyrene as one province. In Augustus's settlement of 27 BC, the Roman historian Cassius Dio lists 'Crete and the Cyrenaic portion of Libya' among the provinces assigned to the Senate, and the Greek geographer Strabo likewise lists Crete with Cyrenaea among the provinces of the Roman people.
